- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.3) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates drop; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for downward correction.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast at 75–78 for next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias (–0.5 to –1.5%) for 7–14 day horizon.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts or price stabilizes.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment confirms upward momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is erratic.
